name: Crucible UB-2 'Umbrella'
description:
A spring-loaded pneumatic dart launcher concealed in the shaft of a full-sized umbrella. The weapon fires a single 5mm steel dart from the umbrella's tip using compressed CO2 stored in the shaft, delivering the projectile with enough velocity to penetrate light clothing and embed 30mm into flesh. The dart can be loaded with chemical payloads — the hollow tip holds 0.3ml of liquid agent — combining the delivery mechanism of the Mercy auto-injector with the range of a firearm.

Crucible designed the UB-2 for intelligence operations during a period of heightened corporate espionage in the 2180s, and the weapon has remained in covert circulation ever since. The firing mechanism is activated by pressing a concealed button on the handle while pointing the umbrella's tip at the target — a gesture that looks like adjusting one's grip or preparing to open the umbrella. The CO2 discharge produces a quiet hiss that is masked by ambient urban noise.

The Umbrella is perhaps the most classically espionage-coded weapon in GLMZ's arsenal — a direct descendant of Cold War assassination tools updated with modern materials and chemistry. Its continued existence is a reminder that some methods of killing are timeless, and that the most effective disguise for a weapon is still 'something everyone carries when it rains.'
specifications:
projectile: 5mm hollow-tip steel dart
capacity: 1 dart
range: 5 meters
propulsion: Compressed CO2
chemical payload: 0.3ml
umbrella length: 85cm
weight: 0.6 kg
acoustic signature: Quiet hiss, masked by ambient noise
tactical_use: Covert assassination and chemical agent delivery at short range. The operator approaches within 5 meters, fires while performing a natural umbrella-handling gesture, and walks away. The dart's small profile and the weapon's silent operation mean the target may not realize they've been hit until the chemical payload takes effect.
cultural_context: The Umbrella weapon has achieved legendary status in GLMZ's intelligence community, partly because of its historical pedigree and partly because it works. In a city where it rains 200 days a year, everyone carries an umbrella. The weapon's disguise is the weather itself.
known_users: Historical connection to at least seven confirmed assassinations in GLMZ
story_hooks: A political figure collapsed during a public appearance on a rainy day. Autopsy revealed a 5mm dart embedded in the thigh, loaded with a neurotoxin. Security footage shows 300 people with umbrellas. The investigation is effectively impossible.
A cache of UB-2 units has been discovered in a Crucible facility that was supposedly decommissioned — along with records of a covert assassination program that spans two decades and three continents.

physical_description.visual_profile: A full-sized umbrella indistinguishable from civilian weather gear — compact canopy, straight shaft, standard handle. The deception is absolute: nothing about its silhouette suggests lethal purpose. Only close inspection reveals the slightly reinforced tip and the barely-visible seam running the length of the shaft where the CO2 reservoir is sealed.
physical_description.dimensions: 85cm total length when closed. Canopy diameter 95cm when open. Shaft diameter 2.2cm. Dart projectile 5mm diameter, 25mm length.
physical_description.weight_description: Slightly heavier than a standard umbrella due to pressurized CO2 cartridge in shaft, but balanced enough to feel natural in hand during casual carry. The extra 0.4kg is distributed along the shaft, so it doesn't tip noticeably.
physical_description.primary_material: Shaft: aerospace-grade aluminum with carbon-fiber reinforcement. Canopy: high-denier nylon with DWR coating. Handle: injection-molded polymer composite with rubberized grip. Firing mechanism: stainless steel and hardened polymer. Projectile: hardened steel with hollow tungsten-carbide tip.
physical_description.finish: Matte black or charcoal nylon canopy with faint water-repellent sheen. Aluminum shaft has a brushed satin finish to avoid reflective glint. Handle is textured black polymer with subtle grip ridges. All metal components are non-reflective — no chrome, no polish.
physical_description.color_scheme: Monochromatic: blacks, charcoals, and brushed silvers. Entirely unremarkable. Could pass for any mass-produced urban umbrella from a corpo supply catalog.
physical_description.grip_texture: Rubberized polymer with fine cross-hatching for positive grip even when wet. Warm to the touch, ergonomic contour. The concealed firing button is flush-mounted on the handle's left side, requiring only thumb pressure to activate.
distinctive_features: Reinforced umbrella tip designed to withstand repeated firing pressure
Barely-visible longitudinal seam along shaft marking CO2 reservoir seal
Flush firing button disguised as part of handle ergonomics — pressure-sensitive, no mechanical click
Dart loading port concealed beneath canopy attachment ring — accessed by unscrewing collar
Micro-engraved serial number inside handle (Crucible marking)
Fine stress marks around the tip from pressurized system
Weight distribution bias toward the shaft — intentional, to feel 'loaded' but not suspicious
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: Crucible Industrial logo (stylized flame symbol) stamped faintly on the inside of the handle. A barely-legible serial plate etched inside the shaft access port. The canopy tag reads 'CRUCIBLE WEATHER SYSTEMS' with a generic model number. Designed to survive cursory inspection as legitimate rain gear.
physical_description.condition_typical: Crucible UB-2s in the field are maintained obsessively — operators know a frayed canopy or visible wear invites scrutiny. Most examples seen are pristine or show only authentic weathering: light water stains, faint scuff marks on the shaft from briefcase carry, minor canopy wear patterns consistent with genuine use. Never visibly modified or battle-scarred; that would defeat the entire purpose.

image_prompt: Product photography of a sleek black umbrella photographed from a three-quarter angle, laid across a dark gunmetal table surface. Dramatic side-lighting casts sharp shadows, emphasizing the reinforced tip and barely-visible shaft seam. Gloved hand (black tactical glove) gently grips the handle, thumb positioned near the concealed firing button. Close-up inset showing the flush-mounted activation point and micro-serial etching. Soft bokeh of rain-streaked urban background. Cinematic neo-noir lighting with cool blue rim-light along the canopy edge and warm amber accent on the metallic tip.
